audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: Quote verified verbatim at the stated locator in the open-text HAL file we hold, and the cross-check locator in the second held HAL file also verified. The deciding source is the primary (and effectively only) field description of Dahalik, by its sole describer; it presupposes stress but states no placement, weight or lexical-contrast rule and says the vowel phonology 'remains to be set up', so not determinable/not stated by the source is the honest coding. Glottolog's whole descriptive bibliography is three items by the same author; web and HAL searches turned up no phonology paper, instrumental study, dissertation or grammar. The only unheld item of note is the 2010 19-pp. sketch (Glottolog Glottolog's most extensive description), print/login-walled, which a contemporary review characterises as verbal-system-focused; obtaining it is worth a medium-priority library request but is unlikely to change the classification. sources.quote: No stress content. Confirms bibliographic facts: Salih Mahmud Idris 'Is Dahalik a dialect of Tigre' pp.113-125; Simeone-Senelle 'The specificity of the Dahalik language within the Afro-Semitic languages' pp.127-145 'bases the specificity of Dahalik mainly on its verbal system and in particular on the use of the verb hade/haddi want as a much used auxiliary'. Series number is Serie Etiopica 8 (Glottolog/HAL say 7).
